Class D learner's permit knowledge test

retake.waitBetweenAttempts: Must wait until the next day to retest
retake.retakeFee: A new learner's permit application fee applies to each attempt

gdl.supervisedHoursRequired: 40 hours (reduced to 30 with an approved Driver Skills Development Program); driver education requires additional supervised hours
gdl.nightCurfew: Junior Operators may not drive 12:30 a.m.-5 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian
gdl.passengerLimits: For the first 6 months, Junior Operators may not carry passengers under 18 unless a licensed driver 21+ is present or the passenger is immediate family

requiredDocuments: Proof of identity and date of birth (e.g. U.S. passport or birth certificate)
Parent or guardian signature if under 18
process.realIdNotes: The RMV issues both REAL ID and Standard credentials. A REAL ID requires one proof of lawful presence, one proof of Social Security number, and two proofs of Massachusetts residency, presented in person.
process.licenseFee: $50 (Class D license); road test fee is $35
process.visionStandard: 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses

facts.pointSuspensionThreshold: Uses surchargeable events, not a point total: 3 surchargeable events in 2 years requires a driver retraining course; 3 speeding tickets in 12 months brings a 30-day suspension
facts.moveOverRule: Move over one lane or slow down for stopped emergency, maintenance, and recovery vehicles displaying flashing lights

bacAdult.display: It is unlawful (operating under the influence, per se) to operate a motor vehicle on a public way with a percentage, by weight, of alcohol in the blood of 0.08 or greater.

conditions.detail: Applies to operators under 21. A breath/blood test result of 0.02 or greater (or a test refusal) triggers an administrative license suspension under the state's zero-tolerance law, independent of any OUI conviction: 180 days for those 18-20, and 1 year for those under 18.

bacUnder21.display: Massachusetts sets a 0.02 zero-tolerance blood alcohol limit for drivers under 21; a result of 0.02 or greater results in a 180-day license suspension (1 year if under 18), separate from OUI charges.

bacCommercial.display: A commercial motor vehicle operator who submits to a test disclosing an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater (or who refuses testing) is disqualified from driving a commercial vehicle for at least 1 year.

conditions.detail: First-offense refusal by a driver 21+ with no priors is a 180-day (about 6-month) administrative license suspension - a civil registry sanction, not a separate crime. The suspension lengthens sharply for repeat offenders or drivers under 21: 3 years (under 21 or 1 prior), 5 years (2 priors), or lifetime (3+ priors).

impliedConsentRefusal.display: Under the implied-consent law, refusing a chemical breath/blood test carries a 180-day administrative license suspension for a first offense (longer for drivers under 21 or with prior OUI offenses - up to lifetime); the refusal itself is not a separate criminal offense.

openContainerProhibited.display: No person may possess an open container of alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on a public way; the driver of any vehicle may never possess an open container. Limited exceptions apply to passengers of for-hire vehicles and the living quarters of a house coach/trailer.

conditions.detail: A first OUI conviction results in a 1-year (365-day) license suspension; the registrar may grant a hardship ('Cinderella') license for work/education after 3 months. Separately, failing a breath test (0.08+) triggers an immediate administrative per-se suspension that lasts until case disposition but no more than 30 days under § 24(1)(f)(2).

duiFirstSuspensionDays.display: A first-offense OUI conviction carries a 1-year license suspension (hardship license possible after 3 months); a failed breath test also triggers a separate immediate administrative suspension of up to 30 days pending disposition.

conditions.detail: Massachusetts law sets NO statutory numeric ceiling for interstates/limited-access highways; MassDOT establishes and posts limits under § 18. 65 mph is the highest limit MassDOT posts anywhere in the Commonwealth (on some rural interstate segments). Where no special limit is posted, the § 17 prima facie limits (e.g., 50 mph on a divided highway outside a thickly settled or business district) apply.

ruralInterstateMaxMph.display: Massachusetts has no statutory maximum interstate speed limit; MassDOT posts limits case-by-case, and 65 mph is the highest posted limit used in the state (on certain rural interstate segments).

conditions.detail: Massachusetts has no separate statutory 'urban interstate' limit; MassDOT posts case-by-case limits under § 18, with 55 mph (or lower) commonly posted on urban/metropolitan interstate segments, e.g., in and around Boston.

urbanInterstateMaxMph.display: There is no distinct statutory urban-interstate limit; MassDOT posts limits under its speed-setting authority, with 55 mph commonly posted on metropolitan interstate segments.

conditions.detail: 30 mph is the prima facie limit inside a thickly settled or business district (the residential default) absent other posting. Outside such districts the prima facie limits rise to 40 mph on an ordinary way and 50 mph on a divided highway.

residentialDefaultMph.display: Absent other posting, the default speed limit inside a thickly settled or business district (residential areas) is 30 mph; it is prima facie evidence of unlawful speed to exceed 30 mph there.

conditions.detail: Applies within a school zone that a city or town has established and posted under M.G.L. c. 85, § 2; exceeding 20 mph in such a zone is prima facie evidence of unlawful speed.

schoolZoneMph.display: In a duly established and posted school zone, exceeding 20 mph is prima facie evidence of driving at a speed greater than is reasonable and proper.

basicSpeedLaw.display: No person may drive faster than is reasonable and proper, having regard to traffic, use of the way, and public safety, and must slow down when a special hazard exists - regardless of any posted limit.

rightTurnOnRed.display: After stopping at a steady red signal, a driver may make a right turn, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic, unless a posted sign at that intersection prohibits the turn.

leftTurnOnRedFromOneWay.display: After stopping at a steady red signal, a driver on a one-way street may turn left onto another one-way street, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic, unless a posted sign prohibits it.

conditions.detail: The seat belt requirement is enforced by police only when the driver has already been stopped for a separate motor vehicle violation or some other offense - i.e., secondary enforcement.

seatBeltEnforcement.display: Massachusetts enforces its adult seat belt law only as a secondary offense: police may cite a belt violation only after stopping the vehicle for another reason.

handheldPhone.display: Under the Hands-Free Law, no operator of any age may hold a mobile electronic device; use is permitted only in hands-free mode. A single tap to activate hands-free mode is allowed, but holding the phone is prohibited for all drivers.

texting.display: No operator of any age may read or view text, images, or video on a mobile electronic device while operating a motor vehicle (a mounted navigation map is permitted); manual texting is banned for all drivers.

moveOver.display: Approaching a stationary emergency vehicle (fire/police/ambulance/disaster), highway maintenance vehicle, or recovery (tow) vehicle displaying flashing lights, a driver must slow to a reasonable and safe speed and, if practicable on a highway with at least two lanes in the same direction, change into a lane not adjacent to the stopped vehicle; no specific slow-to mph is set by statute.

conditions.detail: The statute requires headlights from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise (hence minutesAfterSunset=30), and during any other period when visibility is reduced by atmospheric conditions so as to render further operation without lights dangerous. That weather trigger is a functional low-visibility test, approximated here as whenWipersOn=true; the statute does not literally reference windshield wipers.

headlightsRequired.display: Headlights must be displayed from a half-hour after sunset until a half-hour before sunrise, and at any other time when atmospheric conditions (e.g., rain, fog, snow) reduce visibility enough to make driving without lights dangerous - a functional low-visibility standard rather than a literal wipers-on rule.

state.reason: Massachusetts sets no uniform statewide statutory distance for parking near a fire hydrant. Parking regulation is delegated to cities and towns by M.G.L. c. 40, § 22 (subject to c. 90, § 18 and c. 89, §§ 8-9), so the required clearance is fixed by local ordinance/by-law and varies by municipality; the RMV driver's manual gives only general guidance.

parkFtFromHydrant.display: Not set statewide: Massachusetts leaves fire-hydrant parking clearances to municipal ordinance (M.G.L. c. 40, § 22), so no single statewide distance exists.

state.reason: Massachusetts sets no uniform statewide statutory distance for parking near a crosswalk. Under M.G.L. c. 40, § 22 this is governed by municipal ordinance/by-law and therefore varies by community; there is no single statewide figure.

parkFtFromCrosswalk.display: Not set statewide: crosswalk parking clearances are established by municipal ordinance under M.G.L. c. 40, § 22, so no single statewide distance exists.

state.reason: Massachusetts sets no uniform statewide statutory distance for parking near a stop sign. Under M.G.L. c. 40, § 22 this is governed by municipal ordinance/by-law and varies by community; there is no single statewide figure.

parkFtFromStopSign.display: Not set statewide: stop-sign parking clearances are established by municipal ordinance under M.G.L. c. 40, § 22, so no single statewide distance exists.

state.reason: Massachusetts sets no uniform statewide statutory distance for parking near a railroad crossing. Under M.G.L. c. 40, § 22 this is governed by municipal ordinance/by-law and varies by community; there is no single statewide figure.

parkFtFromRailroad.display: Not set statewide: railroad-crossing parking clearances are established by municipal ordinance under M.G.L. c. 40, § 22, so no single statewide distance exists.

pointSystem.display: Massachusetts does not use a driver-violation point system. Instead it uses a Safe Driver Insurance Plan of surchargeable incidents affecting insurance premiums, plus specific administrative suspensions (e.g., for repeated speeding).

citation.label: M.G.L. c. 175, § 113B
citation.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 175, § 113B (Safe Driver Insurance Plan)

state.reason: Massachusetts has no driver point total, so there is no points-to-suspension threshold. License actions are instead tied to surchargeable events under the Safe Driver Insurance Plan (M.G.L. c. 175, § 113B) and specific offense-based suspensions (for example, three speeding convictions within 12 months lead to a 30-day suspension), not to an accumulated point count.

pointSuspension.display: Not applicable: Massachusetts assesses surchargeable insurance events rather than driver points, so no points-based suspension threshold exists.

citation.label: M.G.L. c. 175, § 113B
citation.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 175, § 113B (Safe Driver Insurance Plan)

permitMinAgeMonths.display: A learner's permit may be issued to any person who is at least 16 years old (192 months).

conditions.detail: Applies to applicants under 18: a junior operator's license requires holding a valid learner's permit for at least 6 months immediately preceding application, with a clean (surcharge-free) driving record during that period.

permitHoldingMonths.display: An applicant under 18 must hold a learner's permit for at least 6 months (with a clean driving record) before qualifying for a junior operator's license.

conditions.detail: A junior operator applicant must complete at least 40 hours of supervised driving, reduced to 30 hours if the applicant completes an approved driver skills development program on a closed, off-road course. This is separate from the driver-education on-road instruction (at least 12 hours driving plus 6 hours observation).

supervisedHoursTotal.display: A junior operator applicant must complete at least 40 hours of supervised driving (30 hours if an approved skills-development program is completed), certified by a parent or guardian.

state.reason: The junior operator licensing statute (M.G.L. c. 90, § 8) requires 40 total hours of supervised driving (30 with an approved skills-development program) but does not carve out a separate statutory minimum number of nighttime supervised hours.

supervisedHoursNight.display: Not applicable: Massachusetts's 40-hour supervised-driving requirement does not include a separate statutory nighttime-hours minimum.

conditions.detail: Junior operator (under 18): the statutory curfew is 12:30 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. startHour24 is rounded from 12:30 a.m. to 0 (midnight) because the schema requires a whole hour - see display for the exact time. Operation between 12:30-1:00 a.m. and 4:00-5:00 a.m. is enforced only secondarily (after a lawful stop).

Learner's permit holder under 18: a stricter permit-phase curfew of 12:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. applies unless accompanied by a parent/legal guardian (or, for an emancipated minor, a licensed driver 21+ with 1+ year experience), per M.G.L. c. 90, § 8B.

gdlNightCurfew.display: A junior operator under 18 may not drive between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian (the 12:30-1:00 a.m. and 4:00-5:00 a.m. windows are secondary-enforcement only). Learner's-permit holders under 18 face a stricter midnight-to-5:00 a.m. curfew. The startHour value is rounded to midnight because the schema stores whole hours.

conditions.detail: During the first 6 months of junior operator licensure, no passenger under 18 may be carried other than an immediate family member, unless a licensed driver at least 21 years old with at least 1 year of driving experience occupies the seat beside the operator.

gdlPassengerPhase1.display: For the first 6 months of a junior operator's license, the holder may not carry passengers under 18 - except immediate family members - unless a licensed driver 21 or older (with 1+ year of experience) is seated beside them.

minLiability.display: For policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2025, the compulsory minimum limits are $25,000 bodily injury per person, $50,000 bodily injury per accident, and $30,000 property damage (raised from the prior 20/40/5 limits by St. 2024, c. 275).

citation.label: M.G.L. c. 90, §§ 34A, 34O
citation.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 90, §§ 34A, 34O (as amended by St. 2024, c. 275, § 4)

conditions.detail: A written crash report to the registrar (and copy to the local police) is required within 5 days whenever a crash results in death, personal injury, or property damage in excess of $1,000 to any one vehicle or other property.

crashReportThresholdUsd.display: A driver must file a written crash report within 5 days if anyone is killed or injured, or if any one vehicle or other property sustains more than $1,000 in damage.
